raw_segments.text: That was a fortnight before this Sunday.
That was why Alyosha had not been to see him, as he had meant to.
But though he waited, he sent Smirov to him twice again.
Both times Krasetkin met him with a curt, impatient refusal, sending Alyosha a message
not to bother him anymore, that if he came himself, he, Krasetkin, would not go to Elisha
Up to the very last day, Smirov did not know that Kalya meant to go to Elisha that morning,
and only the evening before, as he parted from Smirov, Kalya abruptly told him to wait
at home for him next morning, for he would go with him to the Snegaryovs, but warned
him on no account to say he was coming, as he wanted to drop in casually.
Smirov's fancy that Kalya would bring back the lost dog was based on the words Kalya
had dropped that they must be asses not to find the dog if it was alive.
When Smirov, waiting for an opportunity, timidly hinted at his guess about the dog, Krasetkin
I'm not such an ass as to go hunting about the town for other people's dogs when I've
got a dog of my own, and how can you imagine a dog could be alive after swallowing a pin?
Sheepish sentimentality, that's what it is.
